statement: Glia in PD mount a heat-shock and unfolded-protein response (HSP70/HSP90 chaperones up)
our_evidence: Consensus HSP genes up in 5-8 of 8 cell types; HSF1 activation top pathway in all eight; stress-defined states of three studies higher in PD (Figs. 3, 6)

statement: The stress response is shared by many cell types of a patient and across regions, not confined to one cell type
short: shared across cell types and regions
our_evidence: Cell types of a donor correlate (glia r = 0.64-0.73); regions of a donor correlate (r = 0.50-0.83) (Figs. 8, 9)

statement: Neurons do not raise, or repress, chaperones in PD
our_evidence: Chaperones are consensus-up in excitatory and inhibitory neurons; HSF1 activation enriched in neurons (Fig. 3)

statement: Microglia increase in number in PD
our_evidence: Pooled logit share +0.24, 17 datasets, FDR = 0.02; small per study (Figs. 2, 4)

statement: Microglia switch on activation genes in PD (IL1B, GPNMB, SPP1, cathepsins)
our_evidence: Individual activation genes replicate; activation-state signatures only weakly higher (g 0.13-0.21) and track age (Fig. 6)

statement: Inflammatory or activated glial states expand in PD
our_evidence: Inflammatory and activation state signatures of six studies do not separate PD from controls; AR2 astrocytes lower in PD; claims of single states hold in 4 of 14, by the combined test only (Fig. 6)

statement: PD astrocytes become reactive with CD44, GFAP and metallothioneins
our_evidence: CD44 and metallothioneins up in astrocytes across datasets; part of the stress family (Fig. 3)

statement: Oligodendrocytes lose myelinating identity and myelin genes
our_evidence: Myelin-gene loss reproduced as gene-set shifts; consensus down-regulated oligodendrocyte genes (Fig. 3)

statement: Specific disease-associated oligodendroglial subpopulations expand in PD
our_evidence: Proportion claims for subpopulations rarely replicate; the disease-associated oligodendrocyte signature itself is strongly higher in PD (g = 0.95) (Fig. 6)

statement: Dopaminergic neurons are lost from the substantia nigra
our_evidence: Share among nigral neurons −0.56, 6 datasets, p = 0.02; not significant in single studies (Fig. 2b)

statement: The loss is selective for SOX6/AGTR1-positive dopaminergic neurons
our_evidence: AGTR1-positive loss supported; sparing of AGTR1-negative neurons contradicted in 5 of 7 datasets (Extended Data Fig. 9)

statement: T cells infiltrate the PD brain
our_evidence: T-cell shares do not differ consistently; T-cell claims 50% supported (Fig. 2; Extended Data Fig. 4)

statement: Neurons lose synaptic, mitochondrial and metabolic gene expression
our_evidence: Oxidative phosphorylation and DNA repair fall in neurons, lowest where neurons are fewest (Figs. 3, 9)

statement: Cortical neuron composition changes in Lewy-body disease
our_evidence: Excitatory neurons reduced (−0.15, 14 datasets, FDR = 0.02, I² = 4%); inhibitory increases not reproduced (Fig. 2)

statement: Familial PD genes point to dopaminergic neurons
Common-variant PD risk acts through dopaminergic-neuron identity
our_evidence: Not enriched in DA-neuron-specific genes; enriched in oligodendrocyte identity and in genes microglia and vascular cells induce in PD (Fig. 11)

statement: Common-variant risk involves oligodendroglia and microglia
our_evidence: Oligodendrocyte identity p = 0.006; PD-induced genes in microglia, vascular cells and OPCs p = 0.0002-0.006 (Fig. 11)
SNCA claims supported in glia, unresolved in DA neurons (Table S9)
